title: Longest Common Prefix
statement:
Write a function to find the longest common prefix string amongst an array of strings `strs`.

If there is no common prefix, return an empty string `""`.
constraints: strs[i] consists of only lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: The prefix "fl" is common to all input strings.
There is no common prefix among the input strings.

editorial.approach: Horizontal scanning: set prefix = strs[0], then loop over subsequent strings, shrinking prefix length (prefix = prefix.substring(0, prefix.length - 1)) while strs[i].indexOf(prefix) !== 0.
editorial.complexity: O(S) time, where S is sum of all characters in all strings / O(1) space

hints: Assume the first string `strs[0]` is the starting prefix.
Iterate through the rest of the strings. While the current string does not start with the prefix, shorten the prefix by one character from the end.
If the prefix becomes empty, return "" immediately.

bruteForceSolution.explanation: Compare characters column by column across all strings. Stop when a mismatch is found or when the end of any string is reached.
bruteForceSolution.timeComplexity: O(m * n) where m is the shortest string length and n is number of strings

optimizedSolution.explanation: Sort the array alphabetically. The common prefix of the entire array must be the common prefix of the lexicographically first and last strings, reducing comparisons to just two strings.
optimizedSolution.timeComplexity: O(n * m log n) where n is strings count and m is average length (due to sorting)

interviewExplanation: A vertical match comparisons scan takes O(S) time where S is the sum of characters. Alternatively, sorting allows comparing only the lexicographically first and last strings, which is mathematically robust and clean.
